subject: calderMobile
pitch:
Category: Abstract.
Subject: hanging mobile.
Style: Alexander Calder.

spec.name: Calder Mobile
spec.description: A hanging abstract mobile in the manner of Alexander Calder: black wire arms balanced in tiers, hung from a ceiling hook, carrying flat painted sheet-metal leaves and discs in red, yellow, blue, black and white.
spec.layout:
A static, airy kinetic sculpture hanging from a ceiling hook at the top (y 2.4). The lowest tip of the lowest shape touches y=0 and nothing sinks below it by more than 2 cm. Everything is thin: wire radius about 0.005-0.008 and shapes 0.012 thick with a tiny bevel. No two shapes touch. Everything hangs from vertical wires.

Tier 1 (y=2.0): a long straight horizontal black arm A1 along X from x=-1.0 to x=1.0, slung from the ceiling hook by one vertical wire at x=0. Its ends carry small eyelet loops and ball counterweights. Two small flat discs hang directly under it.

Tier 2 left (+X): a medium arm A2 at y=1.5, hung by a wire from A1's left end (x=0.85). A2 is yawed about 32 degrees, direction (0.85,0,0.53), half-length 0.42. One end carries a big red oval. The other end carries a sub-arm A2b with a yellow crescent and a black teardrop.

Tier 2 right (-X): a medium arm A3 at y=1.3, hung from A1's right end (x=-0.85). A3 is yawed the opposite way, direction (0.85,0,-0.53), half-length 0.42. One end carries a sub-arm A3a with a big blue leaf and a small red disc. The other end carries a large black boomerang with a small white disc.

Tier 2 centre: a low arm A4 at y=0.95 along Z, from z=-0.75 to z=0.75. It hangs from the centre of A1 on a long vertical pivot wire at x=0, passing between the two side branches. The front end (+Z) carries a long wire down to a tall blue leaf whose bottom touches y=0. The back end (-Z) carries a sub-arm A4b along X with a red disc and a white rounded triangle.

Balance: the heavy red and black shapes sit near the centre line, small light shapes hang further out. Seen from the front the silhouette is a loose asymmetrical triangle of hanging forms with negative space between them.

Style: Calder's flat primary colours (red, yellow, blue, black, white) on every shape, with black wire and small steel rivets. Shapes are organic cut-out silhouettes (leaves, kidneys, crescents, boomerangs, discs, teardrops), each with a different yaw about Y so the viewer sees some face-on and some edge-on. Each shape hangs from a small steel eyelet loop at its top edge, with a small rivet or clamp where the wire meets the metal. Thin wire is rendered as 6-8 sided sweeps. Every colour is flat, with no paints or textures required.

parts.builds: The top tier. A ceiling rosette (a lathe disc r 0.1, thin, ceiling grey, y 2.36-2.4) with a small steel hook or eyelet ring under it. A thin black wire runs from the hook down to the centre of arm A1 (armA1Center), with a small steel clamp sleeve at the arm. Arm A1 is a straight black wire rod (r 0.008) from x=-1.0 to x=1.0 at y=2.0, with a slightly thicker central collar. Each end has a small steel eyelet loop at x=+-0.85 (armA1LeftEnd, armA1RightEnd) with the top of the downward hanger wire clamped through it, and a small black ball counterweight (r 0.03) at x=+-0.99. Two small flat sheet-metal accents hang directly from A1 on short wires: a yellow disc (r 0.08) centred (0.38,1.80,0), a black disc (r 0.07) centred (-0.45,1.82,0), and a white mini leaf (0.1 tall) at (-0.1,1.78,0.06) hung from the same wire. Discs are extrudes in the XY plane, yawed 20-50 degrees about Y. The long vertical pivot wire runs from armA1Center (pivotDropTop) straight down to armA4Center [0,0.95,0], ending in a small steel eyelet where the centre branch's arm A4 takes it. This part owns that wire (r 0.005) and the clamp. Rivets are tiny steel spheres.
parts.attaches: Hook at ceilingHook, arm A1 centred on armA1Center. The ends armA1LeftEnd and armA1RightEnd are where the left and right branches hang their wires, and the pivot wire ends at armA4Center where centreBranch starts.

parts.builds: The +X branch. A black hanger wire runs from the eyelet at armA1LeftEnd [0.85,2.0,0] down to armA2Center [0.85,1.5,0], with a steel clamp collar. Arm A2 is a black rod r 0.007 centred there, half-length 0.42, direction (0.85,0,0.53), with ball counterweights r 0.022 at both ends and eyelets at armA2EndFront [1.207,1.5,0.223] and armA2EndBack [0.493,1.5,-0.223]. Front end: a vertical wire 0.4 long to a big red kidney/oval, about 0.42 wide and 0.3 tall, with a dark-red (redDeep) small inner disc (r 0.06) layered 5 mm in front as an inset, centred at y~0.92, yawed about 25 degrees. Back end: a vertical wire 0.25 down to the centre of sub-arm A2b at [0.493,1.25,-0.223], a short black rod, half-length 0.3, direction (0.5,0,-0.87). A2b's end hangs a yellow crescent (0.3 wide, with a smooth cut-out arc) on a wire 0.15 long at y~0.95, and its other end hangs a black teardrop (0.12 wide, 0.28 tall) on a wire 0.35 long, with a tiny white disc (r 0.035) dangling below on a thread. Every shape has a steel eyelet loop at its top, a rivet, and an extrude thickness of 0.012 with a bevel. All shape bottoms stay above y=0.4. Everything stays inside x 0.2..1.4.
parts.attaches: Hangs from the crown at armA1LeftEnd. Does not touch centreBranch or rightBranch.

parts.builds: The -X branch. A black hanger wire runs from armA1RightEnd [-0.85,2.0,0] down to armA3Center [-0.85,1.3,0], with a steel clamp collar. Arm A3 is a black rod r 0.007, half-length 0.42, direction (0.85,0,-0.53), with ball counterweights r 0.022 at the ends and eyelets at armA3EndFront [-1.207,1.3,0.223] and armA3EndBack [-0.493,1.3,-0.223]. Front end (-X side): a wire 0.35 down to the middle of sub-arm A3a at [-1.207,0.95,0.223], a short black rod along X, half-length 0.25. It carries a big blue leaf (0.2 wide, 0.5 tall, pointed at both ends, with a thin blueDeep midrib strip layered on it) hung from a 0.1 wire on one end, and a small red disc (r 0.06) on a 0.4 wire from the other end. The lowest bottom is at y~0.3. Back end (-X side toward centre): a wire 0.2 down to a large black boomerang (0.5 wide, 0.2 deep arms, a smooth curved V) hung by its apex at y~0.95-0.7, yawed about 40 degrees, with a small white disc (r 0.05) hung beneath by a thread at y~0.5. Every shape has a steel eyelet at its top, a rivet and 0.012 thickness. Everything stays inside x -1.4..-0.2.
parts.attaches: Hangs from the crown at armA1RightEnd. Does not touch centreBranch or leftBranch.

parts.builds: The low central branch and the floor anchor. Arm A4 is a black rod r 0.008 along Z from z=-0.75 to z=0.75 at y=0.95, hung at armA4Center [0,0.95,0] from the pivot wire the crown ends there. It has a steel clamp collar at the centre, ball counterweights r 0.025 at both ends, and eyelets at armA4EndFront [0,0.95,0.75] and armA4EndBack [0,0.95,-0.75]. Front end: a long wire (0.4) down to a tall blue leaf (0.3 wide, 0.55 tall), a soft almond silhouette with a pointed tip. Its bottom tip touches y=0 (down to -0.015), and its top eyelet is at y~0.55. It carries a yellow disc inset (r 0.07, 5 mm proud) on its face and is yawed about 15 degrees. This is the lowest point of the model. Back end: a wire 0.2 down to the centre of sub-arm A4b at [0,0.75,-0.75], a black rod along X, half-length 0.35, with ball weights. Its +X end hangs a red disc (r 0.11) on a 0.25 wire (bottom ~0.4), with a tiny black disc inset. Its -X end hangs a white rounded triangle (0.22 wide) on a 0.3 wire (bottom ~0.3). All shapes have eyelets, rivets, 0.012 thickness and a bevel. Everything stays within x -0.45..0.45 and z -0.85..0.85.
parts.attaches: Starts at armA4Center, where the crown's pivot wire ends. Stays clear of leftBranch and rightBranch, which are at |x|>=0.2 and mostly above y=0.4.

calls.reasoning:
I'm working out what a hanging Calder mobile should look like in the spec. The pitch says a model placed off the ground keeps its height, but a mobile hangs from the ceiling, so I'm weighing whether its lowest point should sit near the floor. I'm leaning toward putting the lowest point close to y=0 and hanging the whole thing from a top hook at the full height.

I'm settling on the lowest element sitting at y=0, hanging from a top ring near the full height. Then I'm sketching a Calder-style mobile with a ceiling hook, arms balanced on a main wire, and flat colored shapes at the ends, sized about 2.2 wide, 2.4 tall, and 1.6 deep, plainly without joints.

I'm planning the mobile's parts as a tree: a ceiling-hung top arm, then left and right branches hanging from its ends, with a possible third branch from the middle.

I'm now deciding how to split the mobile into parts: a crown with the top arm and small shapes, then left and right branches, and a fourth accent branch hanging from the top arm's middle at a different depth, with the top arm centered at the origin.

I'm laying out the mount points for the mobile now: a top hook at the origin, a main arm centered at height 2.0 spanning about two units along x, and a hanging point for each side arm at x=0.9.

I'm wondering whether the center branch can hang from the top arm without tangling with the right branch, since the wire would pass right by that branch's end. I'm considering a shorter cross arm on the top arm instead, so the center branch sits at a different depth and stays clear of the others.

I'm placing a central drop from the top arm's middle down to a lower arm running along z at about y=0.95, so the mobile's center branch sits clear of the side branches.

I'm splitting the mobile into four parts, starting with the crown: the ceiling hook, canopy, main wire, and the top arm along x with its counterweight beads and small shapes on the ends.

I'm now deciding the crown's contents: the ceiling plate, hook and wire, the main arm with its end loops, and a central pivot wire dropping toward the center branch. I'm also weighing a small black counterweight on top, and I'm leaving the center arm itself to belong to a separate part.

I'm giving the left branch its own wire from the left hang point down to a short arm angled at roughly 35 degrees, centered near x=1.0. Its half-length is around 0.42, which keeps the ends inside the overall width.

I'm checking the width of the second arm's ends, which overshoot, so I'm shifting the left hang point in to x=0.85. That gives the arm ends a span of about 0.49 to 1.21. I'm then placing a red disc hanging from one end and a small sub-arm with two shapes from the other.

I'm now fixing the center branch's arm along z, with its middle at about y=0.95, and setting the rightward and leftward branch hang points and their arms so the parts stay inside the overall box.

I'm sketching the center branch as a long arm along z, with a big blue leaf dropping from its front end to the floor and a smaller sub-arm with two shapes hanging from the back end. I'm checking that these pieces clear the left and right branches, since the shapes there are offset in x.

I'm settling the budget at about 200 per part, so the four parts together stay under 900. To keep the Calder look, I'm adding small details like bolt rivets, eyelet hooks on each shape, and a riveted wire clamp, with flat painted shapes in black, red, yellow, blue, and white. Then I'm checking that the center part owns the floor point, since its lowest shape bottom sits at y=0, while the others stay above it.

I'm settling the front shape so its bottom sits right at y=0, and I'm fixing a colour palette of reds, blues, yellows, black and white, with dark wire and steel greys for the mounts.

I'm sizing the shapes by category and setting their thickness, then I'm varying their yaw so they read well from different angles. Next I'm writing out the crown's bounding box.

I'm checking the crown's width against the new overall box, with the center drop wire running down to the lower arm. I'm also weighing whether the crown should be heavier on one side, then deciding to keep it symmetric. The left and right branch boxes are next, and I'm setting the overall size to about 2.7 wide, 2.4 tall, and 1.7 deep.

I'm checking the right branch's arm ends and their hang points, then fixing the center branch's box along z so its shapes stay inside the overall limits. Next I'm listing the mount points for each part.

I'm placing the left branch's arm at y=1.5, hanging from a wire off the left hang point, with a red oval dropping from one end to about y=1.0 and a wire running down from the other end.

I'm placing the right branch's arm at y=1.3, hanging from a wire off the right hang point, with a blue leaf and a small sub-arm dropping from one end.

I'm placing the center branch's front end at the floor, with a long wire dropping to a large yellow shape, and I'm checking how tall that shape can be before it looks out of proportion with the others.

I'm sizing the center branch's front end: a blue leaf about 0.55 tall, hanging on a wire so its bottom sits at y=0. I'm also weighing a small yellow disc at its center for detail, and then I'm turning to the back end at z=-0.75, where a short wire will drop to a small sub-arm.

I'm placing the back end's sub-arm along x at z=-0.75, with a red disc on one side and a white triangle on the other, then adding a tiny black ball under the disc. Next I'm turning to the crown: a ceiling disc and eyelet, a short wire down to the top arm, and then the arm itself running across the width.

I'm settling the crown's own shapes now: a small yellow disc hung from the top arm near x=0.38, and a small black disc near x=-0.45, both just below the arm. I'm keeping the overall budget in view as I go.

I'm settling the crown's contents and the remaining part budgets, around 790 in total across the four parts. I'm also setting the detail conventions: thin extruded shapes, smooth outlines, eyelet rings at the top, and tiny rivets at the clamps. Last, I'm planning to write the JSON with the shapes oriented by yaw, with y up and the hang wires vertical.

I'm writing buildLeftBranch to take the module's Ctx and destructure it, without importing the type. The plan is static geometry: parts placed directly with no joints, wires made with rods, and shapes built by extruding outlines.

Still working out the helpers and how the shape's thickness axis lines up with its yaw...

I'm shaping the kidney outline's top edge, and a dip at the top would leave the eyelet floating above it. So I'm moving the notch to the bottom so the shape still hangs from the eyelet.

Still working through the kidney outline's bottom notch, so the shape keeps hanging from the eyelet. Then I'm placing the red hanging piece, with its wire dropping to the top edge and its eyelet sitting there. Next comes a small inset disc.

Now I'm placing the inset disc and the rivet on the kidney shape, both offset slightly along its front normal.

Now I'm working out the wire positions for the sub-arm: the two rod ends sit at roughly x 0.64 and 0.34, both at height 1.25. The crescent hangs from one end on a short wire, centred around y 0.95. Then a teardrop goes on a longer wire, its top near y 0.9.

Still working out the crescent's outline and the teardrop's placement on the sub-arm.

Still working out the crescent's outline: the outer arc on the left side, with an inner arc that meets it at the two tips.

Still sorting out the crescent's shape, and whether to stretch it sideways so it has more width.

Still working out the crescent's outline, deciding whether the tips should sit at the top or the side so the eyelet attaches cleanly.

Still working out the crescent's inner edge: I'm sampling points along an inner arc from the bottom tip up to the top tip, then stretching everything sideways a bit so the crescent gets more width.

Still working out the teardrop's outline: a pointed top, then a round bottom built from points on a circle of radius 0.06.

Still working on the eyelet, placing its torus just above the top point and rotating it by the shape's yaw so it lines up with the face. Then the wire from each arm end drops down to the eyelet's top, using thin rods.

Still writing the module's geometry: I'm adding an eyelet-style ring below the arm end, then a hanger rod with a steel collar near the top joint. Next is the main arm rod, running between two points along its direction.

Still checking the spheres and the red piece's spread: the ball sits just beyond each arm end, and the red shape's width puts its far edge right around x 1.4, which is tight but within bounds.

Still checking the sub-arm's bounds: the back end's wire and collar sit at the same spot as before, but the rod's z reach runs past the box edge, so I'm weighing whether to shorten its half-length to 0.25.

Still writing the helper for the disc and the generic hang-shape function, so the disc gets its own thread and eyelet.

Still writing the extrude call for the outlines: I'm passing the outline, its origin and x values, a thickness of 0.012 and a small bevel, with the front face sitting at 0.006.

Still writing the module code: I'm settling the type for the outline points, then setting up the material keys and small helpers for spheres and vectors.
